title: Perfect Discrimination of Non-Orthogonal Quantum States via Adaptive Post-Measurement Queries
summary: A set of pairwise non-orthogonal quantum states cannot be perfectly discriminated, and this remains true even when one bit of classical partial information is available prior to the measurement. Contrary to the usual intuition that earlier information is at least as valuable as later information, we show that the same bit can be more useful when it arrives after the measurement. We present a framework for state discrimination in which the sender provides classical information in response to a request from the receiver, which we refer to as a query.
